oidc-trust.title: Application identity across a trust boundary
oidc-trust.alt: App A obtains an audience-bound token from its issuer or an external issuer. App B resolves the Bearer token, verifies it with trusted issuer keys, creates a stateless application session, and checks IAM permissions.
oidc-trust.caption: A caller obtains an audience-bound token; the callee verifies it before authorization.

oidc-verification.title: From bearer token to an authorization decision
oidc-verification.alt: From bearer token to an authorization decision. Obtain token: OIDCClient.getToken(audience), Cache until expiry minus margin. Resolve bearer: SessionManager tries access token, Then delegates to OIDCVerifier. Match trusted issuer: Decode iss to select configuration, Exact trustedIssuers match. Resolve verification keys: Discovery → jwks_uri → JWKS, Fetch on cache miss / unknown kid. Verify token: Signature, allowed alg, iss, aud, Time claims and configured rules. Authorize operation: Stateless application session, IAM evaluates app principals. IAM evaluates app:<id>, app-issuer:<issuer>, and authenticated-app principals. Issuer selection alone is not authentication: signature and claim verification must succeed.
oidc-verification.caption: A successful OIDC request creates a stateless application session.

compiler-build.title: From TypeScript to an application contract
compiler-build.alt: From TypeScript to an application contract. TypeScript source: src/**/*.ts, Models, services, and operations. Compile: content-mapper build, Emit ES modules to lib/**/*.js. Analyze the program: content-mapper module, Discover model and service metadata. Generate schemas: Model input / output / stored, Service parameter schemas. Write manifest: webda.module.json, Application metadata and schemas. Configuration schema: .webda/config.schema.json, Include dependency manifests. Installed node_modules/**/webda.module.json files also contribute to the configuration schema. Generated artifacts are build outputs: edit the TypeScript source, then rebuild.
compiler-build.caption: Compilation and metadata analysis produce the artifacts used at runtime.

graphql-schema.title: One model definition. A GraphQL schema.
graphql-schema.alt: One model definition. A GraphQL schema.. TypeScript models: Post, User, Comment, Tag, Define fields and relationships. Compiler metadata: webda.module.json, Model JSON schemas. GraphQLService: Read the compiled metadata, Generate the GraphQL schema. GraphQL SDL: Types, queries, mutations, Describe the exposed API. GraphiQL / clients: Use introspection queries, Explore and call the API. The compiler provides model metadata; GraphQLService builds the GraphQL schema from it.
graphql-schema.caption: Model metadata drives the schema exposed to GraphQL clients.

query-translation.title: One query language. Multiple storage backends.
query-translation.alt: One query language. Multiple storage backends.. WQL query: Filter, ordering, pagination, Example: status = published. Parser / validator: @webda/ql · QueryValidator, Build a validated expression tree. Expression AST: AndExpression, ComparisonExpression, and more. MemoryStore: Evaluate expressions per object, In-memory filtering. MongoStore: Translate into a MongoDB filter, Execute against the collection. SQLStore: Translate into SQL predicates, Execute against the database. The three backend paths are alternatives; a query goes to its configured store. Translation support and backend-specific behavior are detailed below.
query-translation.caption: Parse once into expressions; each backend translates or evaluates the result.

benchmark-pipeline.title: Measure, record, compare.
benchmark-pipeline.alt: Measure, record, compare.. Your harness: Create the service under test, Choose its configuration. Shared benchmark suite: benchStore / benchQueue, benchPubSub. BenchmarkRunner: Execute the selected suite, Collect measurements. Result files: bench-results/*.json, Keep comparable run artifacts. Report / compare: webda-bench report, webda-bench compare. Keep workload and environment settings comparable when interpreting benchmark differences.
benchmark-pipeline.caption: A repeatable benchmark pipeline for stores, queues, and pub/sub.

core-architecture.title: Webda runtime: responsibilities and connections
core-architecture.alt: Webda runtime: responsibilities and connections. Application layer: Application / UnpackedApplication, Discover modules; load configuration. Core runtime: Lifecycle and dependency graph, InstanceStorage + core events. HTTP / request layer: HttpServer, Router, WebContext, SessionManager and transports. Services layer: Service + typed parameters, Crypto, binary, domain services. Data layer: Repositories and storage backends, MemoryStore + framework Registry. Shared infrastructure: Logging, metrics, caches, Typed errors across the runtime. These are responsibility groups, not a request sequence; shared infrastructure supports every runtime layer. Models own domain behavior; services coordinate integrations and work across models.
core-architecture.caption: Application configuration becomes a running graph of services and infrastructure.

http-request-flow.title: A request through the runtime
http-request-flow.alt: A request through the runtime. Client → HttpServer: HTTP POST /posts, Receive the request. Router + context: Select the operation handler, Load request identity / session. Operation / domain logic: Validate and authorize input, Invoke model behavior. Repository / store: Persist the model, Return the saved record. Response handling: Write the operation result, Save session state if needed. Client response: HTTP status and response body, 201 Created for a successful create. This illustrates the successful path. Validation, authorization, or persistence errors produce error responses.
http-request-flow.caption: A successful model-create request, from transport to persistence and response.

request-context.title: One request. One shared context.
request-context.alt: One request. One shared context.. Receive request: HttpServer / Router, Headers, cookies, URL, and body. Create WebContext: Attach request and response data, Make context available to handlers. Load session: SessionManager, Resolve the current request identity. Run handler: getInput() / getCurrentUser(), Read the context during execution. Write result: context.write(response), Set status and headers as needed. Finish response: Persist session state if required, Send the HTTP response. Input parsing and validation happen through the context/operation path, not a separate application-wide object.
request-context.caption: WebContext carries input, identity, and the response through the request lifecycle.

service-state-machine.title: The states of a service
service-state-machine.alt: The states of a service. initial: Constructor creates the instance, Synchronous setup only. resolving: resolve() begins, Wire injected dependencies. resolved: resolve() completes, Ready for asynchronous startup. initializing: init() begins, Open connections and start tasks. running: init() completes, Handle requests or background work. stopping: Core.stop() invokes stop(), Release owned resources. stopped: stop() completes, Cleanup has finished. This is the service state machine. Core uses ready for its initialized state and also supports reinitializing. The arrows show ordering, not elapsed time.
service-state-machine.caption: Core manages transitions; service hooks perform the work.

service-startup-order.title: Start in order. Stop together.
service-startup-order.alt: Start in order. Stop together.. Launch application: CLI creates Core(application), Calls Core.init(). Create + resolve services: Construct service instances, Resolve dependencies on demand. Choose init order: Finalize initOrders, Stores before other services. Initialize services: Await init() in the selected order, Connections and background tasks. Run application: Serve requests and operations, Until shutdown is requested. Stop concurrently: Core invokes service stop() hooks, Await their completion together. Shutdown does not promise a service-by-service order. Do not assume another service is still running. Call super.resolve(), await super.init(), and await super.stop() in the corresponding hooks.
service-startup-order.caption: The CLI delegates application startup and shutdown to Core.

model-create-lifecycle.title: Create a model: prepare, authorize, persist.
model-create-lifecycle.alt: Create a model: prepare, authorize, persist.. Create request: REST transport → domain operation, Load and sanitize the input. Prepare model: Build the model instance, Run prepareCreate(context). Authorize create: Check the model permission, Continue only when allowed. Before persistence: Repository emits Create, Listeners receive the model and key. Persist the record: Underlying repository.create(), Write through the configured backend. After persistence: Repository emits Created, Return the saved model to the client. Create and Created are typed repository events; they surround the underlying create operation. The transport returns a successful create response only after the operation completes.
model-create-lifecycle.caption: The successful create path with typed repository events around persistence.

async-queued.title: Queued action execution
async-queued.alt: Queued action execution. Create action: API saves QUEUED in the store. Enqueue: API publishes the action, Worker retrieves the queue item. Start action: Worker saves STARTING, Then asks the runner to execute. Launch job: Runner starts the job, Returns job info to the worker. Save job info: Worker persists runner metadata. Report status repeatedly: Job calls API /async/status, API updates the store. Status callbacks go through the API; the worker handles launch and runner metadata.
async-queued.caption: A queue separates the API from the worker that launches the job.

async-local-hook.title: Local action with HTTP status
async-local-hook.alt: Local action with HTTP status. Create action: Worker saves QUEUED. Start action: Worker saves STARTING. Run action: Worker invokes the runner. Launch job: Runner starts the job, Returns job info to the worker. Save job info: Worker persists runner metadata. Report status repeatedly: Job calls worker /async/status, Worker updates the store. No queue is involved in this flow. Status reports return to the worker over HTTP.
async-local-hook.caption: The worker launches locally and receives the job’s status callbacks.

async-local-store.title: Local WebdaAction execution
async-local-store.alt: Local WebdaAction execution. Create action: Worker saves QUEUED. Start action: Worker saves STARTING. Run action: Worker invokes the runner. Launch job: Runner starts the WebdaAction, Returns job info to the worker. Save job info: Worker persists runner metadata. Report status repeatedly: Job updates the store directly, No HTTP status callback. Direct store reporting is the WebdaAction path; the runner still returns launch metadata to the worker.
async-local-store.caption: A WebdaAction can report its progress directly to the store.

sdk-backends.title: One model client, two backends
sdk-backends.alt: One model client, two backends. ModelClient: Same model API and hydration. Choose backend: Synced model + offline configured? . RemoteBackend: Otherwise: Transport + EntityCache. OfflineBackend: OfflineClient.collection, Local reads and writes. StorageAdapter: IndexedDB or Memory. Sync loop: SyncTransportAdapter → transports, Pull / Push / Snapshot / Watch. Offline sync uses the SDK’s transports and authentication; custom actions still require the server.
sdk-backends.caption: Synced models use local storage; other models use remote transports.

kubernetes-store.title: Models as Kubernetes resources
kubernetes-store.alt: Models as Kubernetes resources. Model definition: Fields and model metadata. Export CRD: webda kubernetes crd export. CRD YAML: CustomResourceDefinition. Application: Model.create / useRepository. KubernetesRepository: CustomObjectsApi. Kubernetes API: kube-apiserver / etcd. Top: install the resource schema. Bottom: create and retrieve model instances at runtime.
kubernetes-store.caption: Export the schema once; use the repository for runtime persistence.

kubernetes-operator.title: Reconcile desired state
kubernetes-operator.alt: Reconcile desired state. Watching: Leader receives changes or resync. Queued: Added or spec changed, One task at a time per object. Reconciling: Run the model’s reconcile(). Finalizing: On deletionTimestamp: finalize(), Remove finalizer to finish deletion. Backoff: On error: delay, then queue again. Update status: Success: observedGeneration + Ready, Return to watching. Success returns to Watching; errors return to Queued after backoff. Deletion follows the finalizer path.
kubernetes-operator.caption: The leader watches changes and serializes reconciliation per object.

bazel-deployment.title: From source to Kubernetes
bazel-deployment.alt: Source and configuration are compiled with webdac. The deployment is applied during packaging. @webda/oci writes app-layer.tar with production files and deployed configuration. oci_image combines it with a pinned Node base. The pod receives environment configuration from a ConfigMap.
bazel-deployment.caption: Bazel compiles and packages Webda; @webda/oci writes the application layer.

traefik-mtls.title: Client certificates through Traefik
traefik-mtls.alt: Client certificates through Traefik. Client certificate: Client starts the TLS handshake. Traefik verifies: Validate against the client CA, Forward the verified certificate. HttpServer checks proxy: Accept only trustedProxies, Reject untrusted forwarding: 400. SessionManager: Read certificate from HttpContext, No Bearer + verified certificate. CertificateProvider: Resolve the user and ident. Stateless session: provider: certificate, amr: mtls. Traefik forwards X-Forwarded-Tls-Client-Cert. Restrict access to the application to trusted proxies.
traefik-mtls.caption: A verified certificate becomes a Webda identity across a trusted proxy boundary.

content-mapper-architecture.title: One transform, two hosts
content-mapper-architecture.alt: One transform, two hosts. Generators + edit plan: accessors / loadParameters, Shared transform implementation. Content mapper: Resident TypeScript Program. Two-pass build: Virtual filesystem. Editor tooling: Hover / rename / diagnostics. Runtime output: .js + .d.ts. Content mappers support the editor. The two-pass build emits JavaScript and declarations for runtime use.
content-mapper-architecture.caption: Shared generators serve editor tooling and the runtime build.
